No kernel feature changes. - Backport #2622: `torch.load(..., weights_only=True)` in `flash_attn/utils/distributed.py` and `flash_attn/models` (CVE-2026-31253 / GHSA-7g5w-pq96-8c5w). #2974 - Backport #2702: safe `tarfile` extraction in `hopper/setup.py` (CVE-2026-62239 / GHSA-w9r7-4gwr-j959). #2974 - Backport #2260: fix int32 overflow in the FA2 backward `dq_accum` offsets, which caused an illegal memory access or NaN gradients when `batch * round128(seqlen_q) * nheads * headdim` exceeded 2^31 (#2987). #2994 - `setup.py`: request cu13 prebuilt wheels for CUDA 13 torch.

items.abstract_or_text: graph: skip the LM head for pooled embeddings (#30445) * graph: skip the LM head for pooled embeddings A context that extracts pooled embeddings outputs one vector per sequence, but every model still expanded its LM head, so the graph computed n_vocab logits per token and the context kept a host buffer for them. The models now only declare t_logits, and set_outputs() expands it unless the context extracts embeddings with a pooling type other than NONE. Since the toggle changes the graph shape for a pooled context, set_embeddings() schedules a re-reserve in that case. * graph: drop the redundant t_embd expand Address review from @CISC: with embeddings on, build_pooling() already expands its output for every pooling type, and a decoder graph without embeddings does not read t_embd, so set_outputs() only expands t_logits. * graph: add build_logits() for the LM head output Address review from @ggerganov: the LM head is expanded by a dedicated build_logits(), called from llama_model::build_graph() like build_pooling(), and set_outputs() only marks the outputs again. * graph: call build_logits() before build_sampling() Address review from @ggerganov: build_sampling() reads t_logits, so the LM head is built first. A pooled context then skips the sampling layers too, since it has no logits to sample from. * nit **Website:** - **Attestations:** - **macOS/iOS:** - [macOS Apple Silicon (arm64)](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/releases/download/b11597/llama-b11597-bin-macos-arm64.tar.gz) - items.abstract_or_text: tests : consolidate context state tests into test-llama-context (#30023) * tests : consolidate the context state tests into test-llama-context test-save-load-state, test-recurrent-state-rollback and test-state-restore-fragmented check the same object from three places: the KV cache and the recurrent state of a llama_context, saved, loaded, copied, rolled back. Each had its own main, its own loop over the models, its own copy of the token and the comparison helpers, and a run of all three loaded the same models several times. They are one binary now, and the case is the unit of the test: tests/llama-context/test-case.h the interface a case implements tests/llama-context/cases-kv.cpp the cases of the KV cache tests/llama-context/cases-rs.cpp the cases of the recurrent state tests/llama-context/test-util.cpp tokens, generation, comparison tests/llama-context/test-runner.cpp the models of a case, on threads tests/llama-context/test-log.cpp the log file of a model A run is a table: a row per model, a column per case, a cell holds the verdict of that pair. The models load on several threads (-j, --threads, min(cores, 4) by default), the table is printed when it is complete and the log of a model that failed is printed after it, in the order of the rows. A case returns a verdict and the reason for it, and the runner is the only one who reports - the test does not use tests/testing.h, a run over 130 models is a matrix of verdicts and not a tree of subtests. Staging no longer travels through the environment: llama_model_set_attn_rot replaces the LLAMA_ATTN_ROT_DISABLE variable, which a model loaded in one thread used to change for the models the other threads were loading, and llama_memory_get_buffers is added for the cases that copy the buffers of a memory. common_log_set_stdo keeps the console quiet while the table is being built. ggml_aligned_malloc allocates with posix_memalign when the thread sanitizer is on. On macOS it allocates with the Mach VM, which the sanitizer does not intercept, so it never sees a page range change hands and reports the first write into recycled memory as a race - 30 of them in this test, and every one of them false. items.abstract_or_text: graph: pad the KV dimension of the no-cache attention to 256 (#30416) The no-cache path builds a [n_tokens, n_tokens] mask and passes K and V unpadded, so FLASH_ATTN_EXT sees K->ne[1] == n_tokens. The CUDA kernels for head size 512 require a multiple of FATTN_KQ_STRIDE, so the op falls back to the CPU for most lengths, and the -fa auto probe (1 token) disables flash attention for such models. Pad the mask like llama_kv_cache::get_n_kv and pad K and V with zeros up to the KV dimension of the mask. clef builds its own causal mask and pads it the same way. **Website:** - **Attestations:** - **macOS/iOS:** - items.abstract_or_text: metal : fix mul_mat_id with duplicate ids (#30373) * metal : fix mul_mat_id limits and kernel name * metal : fix mul_mat_id with duplicate ids kernel_mul_mm_id_map0 assumed at most one match per token and a fixed capacity of ne21 entries per expert, which produced wrong or dropped output rows and could overflow into the slice of the next expert when the ids contain duplicates. build a compact per-expert list of the (token, slot) entries instead: - pass 1 counts the entries of every expert, thread 0 computes the offsets of the expert slices (tpe now holds [base, count]) - pass 2 writes the entries with one unconditional store per token (conditional stores of divergent lanes are very slow), the dummy value of the tokens without a match lands on a padding slot of the slice that is never read - duplicates are handled by a rare branch - kernel_mul_mm_id reads the base/count of its expert and loops over the entry tiles that do not fit into the grid The ids buffer is sized as ne20*ne21 + ne02 (entries + padding). 883/883 test-backend-ops MUL_MAT_ID tests pass, llama-bench is within run-to-run variance of the previous behavior. Assisted-by: pi:llama.cpp/MiMo-V2.6-Flash-MOPD * metal : make mul_mat_id map0 ne02 a function constant use FOR_UNROLL for the id loops of kernel_mul_mm_id_map0 and turn ne02 into the function constant FC_mul_mm_id_map0_ne02 (FC_MUL_MM + 7), so that the threadgroup offsets of cnt/bas/sids and the prefix-sum bound fold at compile time. the pipeline name now encodes ne02 (same convention as the ssm_conv nc/silu constants) and the map0 pipeline is compiled with the constant value set. ne02 is no longer part of ggml_metal_kargs_mul_mm_id_map0 - the dispatch grid still comes from the tensor ne[2] on the host. no measurable perf change: 883/883 test-backend-ops MUL_MAT_ID tests pass, op-level and llama-bench results are within run variance. Assisted-by: pi:llama.cpp/MiMo-V2.6-Flash-MOPD * cont : clean-up + TODO * metal : dispatch mul_mat_id entry tiles from the prepass follow the approach of the vulkan implementation (#29998): instead of launching a grid over experts x ne21 entry tiles and letting most of the threadgroups early exit, kernel_mul_mm_id_map0 now also emits a row map - the total tile count plus one (expert, first entry, valid rows) descriptor per 32-entry tile that has work. kernel_mul_mm_id is launched with a static upper bound on the number of tiles (full tiles over all entries plus at most one partial tile per expert), reads its descriptor and processes a single tile - the tail early exits. This removes the round loop that was needed to cover duplicate ids past the grid (register pressure: th_max 768 -> back to the plain mul_mm level) and duplicates are now handled implicitly, since they only produce more descriptors within the bound. The grid shrinks by ~8-16x on typical shapes (e.g. 128 experts, 8 used, 512 tokens: 128 tiles instead of 2048 entry tiles, of which 94% only launched to exit) and ne21 is no longer needed by the mm kernel kargs. 883/883 test-backend-ops MUL_MAT_ID tests pass. llama-bench (Qwen3.6-35B-A3B Q8_0) is now faster than master on all pp sizes (pp2048/4096/8192 +2%, pp512 +0.5%), tg32 unchanged. Both counters are reported on one line in the perf stats.
